title: How Are the Seven Chakras Usually Listed?
h1: How Are the Seven Chakras Usually Listed?
excerpt: The usual English list runs from root to crown with Sanskrit names. It is a modern teaching order, not the only historical list.

quick_answer.question: How are the seven chakras usually listed?
quick_answer.answer: From the base of the spine upward, popular charts list root, sacral, solar plexus, heart, throat, third eye, and crown, with the Sanskrit names muladhara, svadhisthana, manipura, anahata, vishuddha, ajna, and sahasrara.

intro: The list is worth knowing because studios assume it. It is not worth believing as anatomy. The order is a teaching convenience.

sections.heading: What is the usual order?
sections.content:
Root is muladhara, sacral svadhisthana, solar plexus manipura, heart anahata, throat vishuddha, third eye ajna, and crown sahasrara. Center pages give locations used in the modern chart. Colors in the rainbow sequence are a later overlay. Older sources do not all count seven or stop at these jobs.

The neighboring page is [the root chakra page](/chakras/root-chakra/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: What do the Sanskrit names mark?
sections.content:
Hatha and tantric literature discuss centers and syllables with more variation than a poster allows. Twentieth-century writers stabilized the seven-part chart for new readers. The explainer and the science page tell that history.

A wider map lives at the [chakras topic](/topics/chakras/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: What does the list not settle?
sections.content:
Learn the names so a class is intelligible. You can ignore the emotional slogans. You can practice without using the list at all. Stones and affirmations are not part of the classical count.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [what chakras are](/articles/what-are-chakras/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not use the list to diagnose illness or character. Do not assume a color is traditional just because it is familiar. The chart is a map of a teaching, not of your organs.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Seven names are the popular literacy list.
The list is not a medical exam.

faq.question: Must I start at the root?
faq.answer: Only if you are following a teacher who says so. The requirement is not a fact of anatomy.

faq.question: Is this a full guide?
faq.answer: No. It answers one question and points to the longer page. It is not personal instruction or medical advice.
